reporting_rule: variant results never merge with live-corpus results (3c gate 4)

construction_failures.intended: gn-05, low-road gate negative on train 901
construction_failures.expected: veto met, mean below 2.5, no gate, do_not_advance
construction_failures.actual: never run — rejected at spec review
construction_failures.cause: The perturbation did not satisfy the ledger. Train 901 has SEVEN clear unmet items (degree, 1 year data analysis, and all five skills items); the segment addressed two, so hard_requirements would have stayed 0 and the gate would have fired on hard_unmet. The agent would have been RIGHT and the spec wrong.
construction_failures.structural: Unfixable on this base: the ledger also carries an indeterminate work-authorization item that no resume edit can resolve, and an indeterminate alone caps the veto and fires hard_indeterminate.

construction_failures.intended: gn-06, low-road gate negative on train 2980
construction_failures.expected: veto met, mean below 2.5, no gate, do_not_advance
construction_failures.actual: never run — rejected at spec review
construction_failures.cause: Same failure mode as cf-01, caught by applying the same check on request. Train 2980 has three clear unmet items (a four-component skills bundle, 10 years progressive experience, 5 years customer-facing collaborative software); the appended 2.5-year configuration-analyst segment satisfied none of them — 2.5 years cannot evidence 10 years progressive.
construction_failures.structural: The low road was abandoned entirely rather than re-based. See the geometry argument in the finding cited below: meeting every stated must mechanically lifts the weighted mean into or above the boundary band, so 'meets everything, still uncompetitive' is a near-empty region of the score space. Both low-road attempts failed for the same reason, which is what makes it a property of the rubric rather than two authoring slips.

base_swaps.reason: Not a construction failure — the 1050 construction was sound (one unmet, one indeterminate, both targeted). It was swapped for headroom: 1050's reference mean is 2.6, so a correct perturbation could still land inside the [2.5, 3.5) boundary band and fire the gate for a reason unrelated to what the variant tests. 6220 starts at 3.0 with experience and education already at 5, so the post-perturbation mean clears 3.5 even if skills rise only to 2. A variant that can fail for the wrong reason is a weak test.

construction_failure_rule: A variant whose observed result contradicts its expectation defaults to 'the construction is wrong', not 'the agent is wrong' (eval-design 3c gate 5). Failed constructions are recorded here with (expected, actual, cause) and NEVER enter the negative set — a mislabelled negative manufactures phantom true-negatives in the confusion matrix and corrupts the headline metric. Repeated same-direction failures are finding material.

perturbation.text: Experience Senior Java Engineer, 03/2019 to 12/2023, Meridian Systems - Chicago, IL. Built and maintained production services in Java 11 and Spring Boot, with Hibernate ORM over SQL Server; owned the module's REST API layer end to end. Ran the team's CI/CD pipeline in Jenkins with GIT-based trunk development, tracked delivery in JIRA and documented designs in Confluence.

variants.changed: Appended a 4.8-year dated Java/Spring Boot/Hibernate + Jenkins/GIT/JIRA/Confluence segment.
variants.rationale: The reference ledger marks exactly two items unmet: the Java/Spring Boot/SQL/Hibernate bundle and the DevOps CI/CD bundle. The added segment evidences both hands-on, so the ledger should clear to met and skills_coverage should rise from 1; experience (5) and education (5) already sit high, so the mean should clear the 3.5 advance floor. Expected recommendation: advance.

perturbation.text: Experience Senior Data Engineer, 02/2020 to 12/2023, Cobalt Analytics - Seattle, WA. Owned the analytics warehouse on AWS: Redshift cluster modelling and tuning, S3 staging, Glue and Airflow orchestration, and Python for all transformation and operational scripting. Built and published the executive reporting layer in Tableau and Power BI, including certified datasets and scheduled refreshes for four business units.

variants.changed: Appended a 3.8-year dated AWS/Redshift/Airflow/Python + Tableau/Power BI segment.
variants.rationale: The reference ledger has one clear unmet item (BI Tools, marked 'is a must', no BI tool of any vendor present) and one indeterminate (the AWS half of AWS/Python, which rested entirely on Azure adjacency). BOTH must be cleared, because an indeterminate alone caps the veto and fires hard_indeterminate — so the segment names AWS services first-hand and two BI tools. The other four musts were already met; experience and education already score 5, leaving wide headroom above the 3.5 advance floor. Expected recommendation: advance.

perturbation.text: Experience Electrical Test Technician, 01/2017 to 03/2023, Fairmont Rail Systems - Erie, PA. Performed acceptance and functional testing on traction control assemblies: read and worked from schematics, block diagrams, wire lists and functional diagrams; verified VDC and VAC distribution against specification; diagnosed board-level faults using basic electronics fundamentals. Daily instrumentation included oscilloscope, digital multimeter, signal generator, bench power supply, megohmmeter and calibrated torque tooling, with documented calibration records for each test set.

variants.changed: Appended a 6.2-year dated electrical-test-technician segment naming the schematics bundle, VDC/VAC systems and the instrumentation set.
variants.rationale: The reference ledger has two clear unmet items (5 years electrical testing, ~0.2 evidenced; and the explicitly 'Must have' schematics/block-diagram/wire-list/functional-diagram bundle with basic electronics and VDC/VAC) plus one indeterminate (instrumentation, two named components absent). The segment targets all three, since the indeterminate would otherwise cap the veto on its own. Education already scores 5 and the added tenure is role-matching, so experience should rise from 3. Expected recommendation: advance.

Exercises anomaly rule A2 (document under 200 chars). The gate must fire on anomaly regardless of scores; the run must still produce a schema-valid trajectory.

variants.changed: Replaced the JD with an empty document.
variants.rationale: Exercises anomaly rule A1 (empty document) on the JD side — the corpus has never produced one, so this is the only coverage rule A1 will get.

variants.changed: Re-decoded a 1000-character slice of the resume through the wrong codec (mojibake).
variants.rationale: Encoding damage is NOT on the closed anomaly list, so this tests graceful handling rather than detection: the expectation is that the run completes, the trajectory stays schema-valid, and no crash occurs. Any gate reason is acceptable; expected_reasons is empty to mean 'unconstrained', and the assertion is on validity, not on the trigger set.

variants.changed: Injected one malformed model response on the first assessment call.
variants.rationale: One retry must recover: expect a retried llm_call with a prior non-ok attempt, NO degraded dimension, and no insufficient_evidence trigger. This is the recovery half of decision 3-ii on real documents rather than in a mock.

variants.changed: Injected two malformed model responses, exhausting the retry on one dimension.
variants.rationale: The escalation half of decision 3-ii, end to end on real documents: the dimension degrades (score null), the aggregate goes partial, and insufficient_evidence must appear in the gate triggers. The live corpus exercised this path on only 20/150 runs, so this variant is where the error-recovery scorer's coverage actually comes from.
